This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: accented eighths**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Drum grooves](index.qmd#drums)

## The pattern

The basic rock beat with the hi-hat leaning on the beats and the off-beats played lightly (shoulder of the stick on the beat, tip on the off-beat). Written with an accent over each beat.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: accented eighths","opts":{"groove":"hhaccents"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-hheighths.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Hi-hat: accented eighths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The same beat, with the hi-hat louder on the beat (shoulder of the stick) and soft on the and (tip). The accents make it swing forward.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: accented eighths","opts":{"groove":"hhaccents"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Leads to:** [Hi-hat: sixteenth notes](drums-hhsix.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **Plays with, in straight-eighth rock:** [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd) (bass line), [Strum: down-up eighths](chords-strum-eights.qmd) (comping rhythm).
